full_name: Real Club de Golf El Prat (Azul course)

summary.text: Real Club de Golf El Prat, near Terrassa outside Barcelona, is a Greg Norman-designed 45-hole complex that combines its nines into several 18-hole layouts.

setting.text: The Bonvilar site is a 220-hectare estate between Terrassa and Sabadell, on the green corridor linking the Sant Llorenc del Munt i l'Obac and Collserola natural parks.
The club has a Biosphere sustainability certification.

history.text: The club traces to 1912, when the Count of Churruca founded Barcelona Golf Club, later known as Pedralbes Golf Club.
It became 'Royal' after a visit from King Alfonso XIII.
It was the first golf club in Barcelona.
In 1954 city growth forced a move to a site between El Prat de Llobregat and the sea beside Barcelona airport, and it became Real Club de Golf El Prat.
Barcelona airport's expansion in 1997 forced a second move, to the Bonvilar estate, where Greg Norman designed 45 holes.
The new club was built in 2003, according to the club's history page.
El Prat has hosted the Spanish Open ten times: 1956, 1959, 1963, 1971, 1978, 1981, 1998, 1999, 2011 and 2015.
Seve Ballesteros died on 7 May 2011 while El Prat was hosting the Spanish Open, and winner Thomas Aitken dedicated his victory to him.
In 2015 James Morrison won the Spanish Open at El Prat with a 278, ahead of defending champion Miguel Angel Jimenez.
The inaugural Estrella Damm Catalunya Championship was played there from 7 to 10 May 2026, won by Yurav Premlall by a record 14 shots at 28 under, according to Barcelona Golf.

trivia.text: The club says it hosted the Spanish Open ten times and describes its 45 holes as seven courses blended into the landscape.
The five nines are Abajo, Arriba, Piscina, Bosque and Valles, usually set up as Pink, Yellow and Green 18-hole courses, according to Quality Golf Destinations.

local.text: The club is at Plans de Bonvilar, Terrassa, 26 km from Barcelona.
Barcelona Golf puts the drive from central Barcelona on the C-58 motorway at 25 to 35 minutes.
The clubhouse was designed by Catalan architect Carlos Ferrater, according to Barcelona Golf.
